clue.text: Regard displaced persons, noble at heart, as little treasures

parts.note: to regard something is to see it

indicators.note: the noble sits in the heart of the persons, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: DPs is the standard abbreviation for displaced persons, refugees after the war
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone views refugees, with a nobleman among them, as precious little ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced persons' looks like part of the surface story of refugees, but is the abbreviation DPs; 'at heart' places the noble in its middle, making DPEARLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed pearls are tiny pearls, small precious items used in jewellery.

clue.text: Sucker I would describe as tasty

parts.note: a sap is a gullible person, a sucker
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A fool says he would call something delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having a pleasant flavour, savoury.

clue.text: May offhand expert love me madly ?

indicators.note: acting madly, the letters are thrown into a crazy new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Might an expert in passing fall wildly in love with me?
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means done without preparation, impromptu.

clue.text: Brotherhood of Victorian naturalists

parts.note: reads as a club of nature-lovers, but means an art movement founded in 1848 committed to truth to nature

explanation.surface: A society of nineteenth-century nature-lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naturalists' suggests birdwatchers or botanists; here it means painters devoted to faithful depiction of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood was a group of Victorian painters, including Rossetti and Millais, devoted to detailed natural realism.

clue.text: Pause, perhaps, about one hundred — it's an omen

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes round the other letters
perhaps says the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A break of around a hundred seconds is taken as a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PAUSE into AUSPE; 'about' puts it round IC.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is a sign or portent, originally from observing birds.

clue.text: Leave for the wedding

parts.note: reads as time off work to attend, but means the official permission needed to marry

explanation.surface: Time off to go to a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage licence is the legal permission, or leave, to wed.

clue.text: Little Abraham died in his cot

parts.note: Abe is the short form of the name Abraham
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A small boy called Abraham has died in his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sad death, but 'in his cot' is the definition of lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in his cot is lying in bed, an adverbial phrase for the same state.

clue.text: Fish caught right in the beam

indicators.note: the right letter goes in the beam, one piece inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish is landed straight into the boat's timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside BEAM; 'caught' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream are freshwater or sea fish of the carp and sea-bream families.

clue.text: The craft of Siva

parts.note: Siva is the Hindu god of destruction, so his trade is destroying, and a craft can also be a warship

explanation.surface: The skill of a Hindu god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests skill, but is a vessel; Siva is the destroying member of the Hindu trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Siva bears the title of the Destroyer, and a destroyer is a fast warship.

clue.text: Masterpiece of artist rejected by 3

parts.note: the brotherhood at 3 down named itself against the art of Raphael, whose famous Virgin and Child painting is meant

explanation.surface: A great painting by a painter the brotherhood spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: The brotherhood at 3 down rejected Raphael's influence; his best-known Madonna was painted for the church of San Sisto in Piacenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael's Sistine Madonna, now in Dresden, is one of the most famous Renaissance paintings.

clue.text: Leg-wound bandages for old soldiers

parts.note: reads as dressings for injured veterans, but means strips of cloth wound round the leg that soldiers once wore

explanation.surface: Dressings for the leg injuries of veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg-wound' looks like an injury to the leg; it means wound (wrapped) round the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Puttees were long cloth strips wrapped spirally round the lower leg as part of army uniform.

clue.text: The tools of cheats

definitions.meaning: carpenter's cutting implements with a bevelled blade
to swindle someone, a slang verb

explanation.surface: The kit that swindlers use.
explanation.definitionFit: Chisels are woodworking blades, and to chisel someone is slang for cheating them.

clue.text: Curse the mother-country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone swears at their motherland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother-country' looks like one idea, motherland, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is used as an exclamation or oath, a curse.

clue.text: Water-front of the Duchy

parts.note: the Duchy is Cornwall, and the river forming its border with Devon is a front made of water

explanation.surface: The seafront of a duke's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchy is Cornwall, the English county held by the Duke of Cornwall; the river Tamar runs along almost its whole eastern boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is the river dividing Cornwall from Devon, so it is the county's watery frontier.

clue.text: Irish boy's soup

definitions.meaning: from the Irish phrase for a fine lively lad, 'a ___ of a boy'
a thin soup made from stock

explanation.surface: A young Irishman's bowl of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin soup, and a lively Irish lad is 'a broth of a boy'.

clue.text: Iron for example as a foundation ?

definitions.text: Iron for example as a foundation ?

parts.words: Iron for example as a foundation ?
parts.note: iron is an example of a common non-precious metal, and base means foundation

explanation.surface: Is iron used as a building's footing?
explanation.definitionFit: A base metal is a common, non-precious one such as iron, while base also means a foundation.

clue.text: Eastern flyer is on our side always

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, a flyer
an ally is someone on our side

explanation.surface: A pilot from the East has always been a friend to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for ever, at all times.

clue.text: Bring down a pack of forecastle hands

parts.note: to lower is to bring down
a deck is a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Fell a gang of sailors from the front of the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower deck means the ratings of a navy ship, the crew quartered forward rather than the officers.

clue.text: Little Stephen the artist acts as loader

parts.note: Steve is the short form of Stephen
Gustave Doré was a French illustrator

explanation.surface: Young Stephen the painter works as a docker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at the docks.

clue.text: Oration that is out of order in Canada

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are not in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A speech that breaks the rules of debate in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' suggests a ruling by the Speaker, but rearranges ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a province in Canada, a place in that country.

clue.text: Turn out on football team

parts.note: to evert is to turn inside out

explanation.surface: Turn up to watch a soccer side.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a football club in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton FC is an English professional football club.

clue.text: One man, accompanied by his dog

definitions.text: One man, accompanied by his dog

parts.words: One man, accompanied by his dog
parts.note: recalls the counting song 'One man went to mow, went to mow a meadow, one man and his dog'

explanation.surface: A lone man walking with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery counting song 'One man went to mow' ends each verse with 'one man and his dog', so that one man is the one who mows.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song the single man with his dog goes out to cut a meadow, so he is the grass-cutter.

clue.text: New Zealander is the right one to follow the chairman

indicators.note: the right one comes after the chairman, so these letters are placed behind his

parts.note: Chairman Mao led the Chinese Communist Party
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Kiwi is the proper person to succeed the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people native to New Zealand.

clue.text: An artist or a writer

parts.note: a pen is the instrument that writes

explanation.surface: Someone is either a painter or an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests a person but is the pen that writes; Sir William Orpen was an Irish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Orpen was a noted portrait painter and war artist.

clue.text: The order holds nothing for a great king

indicators.note: the order and its article contain the nothing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The religious order has nothing to offer a mighty monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The order' reads as a religious order, but is the architectural Doric order; 'holds' sets the zero between the article and the order's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodoric the Great was the Ostrogoth ruler of Italy around 500 AD.

clue.text: Call for a pint in the vault

parts.note: to cry is to call out
pt is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a beer down in the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vault beneath a church.

clue.text: Hats for the fast set ?

parts.note: headwear is clothing worn on top, and the fast setting in a car's gearbox is the highest

explanation.surface: Headwear for fashionable racy people.
explanation.walkthrough: Hats are gear for the top of you; the 'fast set' is not trendy people but the car's highest ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: Top gear is a car's highest gear for speed, and the phrase can also mean clothing for one's head.

clue.text: Skin-treatment centre

parts.note: reads as a beauty clinic, but means a works where animal hides are cured into leather

explanation.surface: A clinic for complexion care.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is where hides are turned into leather by soaking in tannin.

clue.text: Advanced the time for abstention

definitions.meaning: to have advanced money is to have loaned it
the forty days before Easter, when Christians give things up

explanation.surface: Moved forward the season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced is money loaned, and the Christian fasting season before Easter has the same name.

clue.text: Where to buy cereals in Oxford Street

definitions.meaning: a market where grain is sold
a main shopping street in the centre of Oxford

explanation.surface: Shopping for breakfast grains on a London high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford Street' suggests London's famous shopping street, but it is a street in the city of Oxford: Cornmarket Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn market sells grain, and Cornmarket is a well-known street in central Oxford.
